title: Referrals and repeat work from existing clients for hard floor care
audience: Owners of hard floor care businesses who want repeat maintenance work and referrals from homeowners, property managers and businesses they have already served.
learningOutcomes: Plan a review or referral request that is made after the client confirms the result and that the client can decline easily.
Write a next-service offer with a date, a scope and a price approach, and schedule the check-in that follows it.
Write referral reward terms, including the condition for payment, before any referral is made.

instruction.heading: Ask once the client has confirmed the result
instruction.body: Ask for a review or referral after the client has confirmed that the floor looks right, usually at sign-off or when the invoice is paid. Use one sentence, name the next step and make it easy to decline. One Baylor Keller Center experiment found that a late reminder drew more reviews than an immediate one; that is one experiment. The AMA says the best timing depends on the product, and that experience goods need more time to evaluate. A polished floor may need several days before a client judges the result, so test the timing with your own clients.

instruction.heading: Ask every client, and use the review link
instruction.body: Google provides a review link or QR code that you can share. Ask every client, not only the ones you expect to praise. Filtering who is asked is review gating, which the vendor Podium says Google treats as a violation (not checked against Google's policy). Never write reviews for clients or invent them. Google bans discounts or goods in exchange for reviews. The ACCC says incentives must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says (15 July 2026).

instruction.heading: Offer a maintenance schedule in writing
instruction.body: At sign-off, propose a maintenance visit with a date and an interval, such as a clean and a maintenance coat at a set interval, or a visit before a busy season. The intervals are illustrative choices. The research found no repeat-work or maintenance-plan evidence for hard floor care. Write the scope, the interval and the price approach, and get the client's confirmation before you change the schedule. A short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan is one approach a vendor recommends (Housecall Pro, 8 June 2026). Define in the terms how any unused visit rolls over, because the research found no source for that rule.

instruction.heading: Re-contact property managers and strata managers carefully
instruction.body: Property managers and strata managers may book floor work for common areas. The research did not find a source for those channels, so treat them as untested. Plan a short factual message before a busy period you can deliver, offer only slots you can deliver, and keep it optional. Honour every opt-out within five working days (ACMA).

instruction.heading: Set referral rewards in writing before anyone refers
instruction.body: Decide the reward and write the payment condition, usually that the referred client has booked and completed a paid job. Stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referrals across the studies that Xu, Yu and Tu report (2023). Get the referred person's consent before any message goes to them (Clayton Utz, 2017, older source). Tax and contract effects of a credit were not confirmed, so take advice before you start.

procedure: After each job is signed off, make one review or referral request, and record what was asked and the answer.
Write the maintenance offer with a date, scope, interval and price approach, and get the client's confirmation.
Schedule the check-in at an interval you have tested, and send it under the electronic message rules.
Plan re-contact before each busy period you can deliver, and leave out anyone who has opted out.
Write the referral reward and its payment condition before the first referral is made.
When a referral books and is paid, apply the reward and record the outcome.
Review each season which requests, offers and timings produced repeat work.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A floor-care operator polished a homeowner's timber hallway and lounge room. The owner says she will recommend the operator to a friend with a similar floor, and asks whether she can get a discount on her next maintenance visit in return.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the operator write down before the friend is contacted, and what should be avoided?
workedExamples.reasoning: The operator writes the terms first: the discount on the homeowner's next maintenance visit, the payment condition (the friend books and completes a paid job) and the date the discount applies. The homeowner passes on the friend's details, and the operator contacts the friend only after she agrees. The operator does not offer the discount for a review, does not tie any reward to what a review says, and does not promise an amount that is not in writing. If the discount has a tax or contract effect, the operator takes advice before starting. The operator accepts only the work that the operator's licence and insurance cover.

equipmentAndPpe: Client record with the sign-off date and the review or referral request made
Next-service offer template with scope, interval and price approach
Calendar of seasonal re-contact dates for the service
No PPE is needed for client follow-up; any site visit follows the site's own safety rules

commonErrors.error: Asking for a review before the client has confirmed the floor looks right.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask at sign-off or after payment, once the result is confirmed.

commonErrors.error: Offering a referral discount that was never written down.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the reward and its payment condition before any referral, and give the client a copy.

commonErrors.error: Filtering which clients are asked for a review.
commonErrors.prevention: Ask every client, and let the review link do the rest.

commonErrors.error: Using a client's floor photos in marketing without consent.
commonErrors.prevention: Get consent for each use, and keep the record.

commonErrors.error: Contacting a client who asked not to hear from you.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep an opt-out list and act on each request within five working days.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Publishing a client's name, photo, review or property detail needs the client's consent for that use. If the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) applies to your business, check the OAIC direct-marketing guidance (modified 5 September 2024). Whether the Act applies was not confirmed.

Check-in and re-contact messages by email or text can be commercial electronic messages under the Spam Act 2003 (Cth). A message that promotes any service can be commercial even when framed as a reminder (Clayton Utz, 2023).
Review platforms and referral schemes have their own rules on incentives. Check each platform's rules, and the ACCC's statement that incentives must be disclosed, before offering any reward.

A referral does not extend the licence or insurance of the business that accepts the work. Accept only the work your licence and insurance cover, in the state or territory where the work is done. Licence rules for hard floor work were not researched.

qualityStandard: Every review or referral request is made after sign-off or payment, and it includes an easy way to decline.
Every next-service offer is written, has a date and is confirmed by the client before the schedule changes.
Every referral reward has written terms and a payment condition, and is paid only when that condition is met.
documentationEvidence: Review or referral request log with the date sent and the answer.
Next-service offers with the date, scope, interval and client confirmation.
Referral reward terms with the referral record and payment outcome.
summary: Ask for reviews and referrals after the client has confirmed the floor, and make it easy to decline.
Offer the maintenance visit in writing, with a date, before the client leaves.
Set referral terms and payment conditions in writing before anyone refers. Gaps: no floor-care repeat-work evidence and no property or strata referral source was found.

knowledgeChecks.question: When is the best time to ask a client for a review or referral?
options: Before the work starts, so the client feels committed
After the client has confirmed the floor looks right
Only after the client has made a complaint

knowledgeChecks.question: A client wants to post a review with her name and photos of her floor. What do you need?
options: Her consent for that name and those photos
Nothing, because the review is positive
Your own view that the photos look good

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a referral reward look like?
options: Paid to anyone who mentions your name
Decided after the referred person books, based on how keen the referrer seems
Written in advance, with the payment condition stated

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a maintenance visit be proposed to a client?
options: At sign-off, with a date and a scope

sourceReferences: Baylor Keller Center, 'Wait Just a Minute', https://kellercenter.hankamer.baylor.edu/news/story/2024/wait-just-minute-when-ask-online-reviews, 1 June 2024 (metadata says 13 May 2024). One experiment only. Supports: an immediate reminder reduced reviews and a later reminder raised them.

American Marketing Association, 'Asking for customer reviews at the right time', https://www.ama.org/2023/01/10/asking-for-customer-reviews-at-the-right-time-sooner-is-not-always-better/, 10 January 2023. Supports: the right timing depends on the product; experience goods need more time to evaluate.

Google Help, Business Profile review help page, https://support.google.com/business/answer/3474122?hl=en-GB, no date shown. Supports: a review link or QR code may be shared; discounts or goods in exchange for reviews are banned.

Podium, 'Review gating', https://www.podium.com/article/review-gating, 2 May 2022. Vendor source; its account of Google's position was not checked against Google's policy. Supports: filtering who is asked for a review is called review gating.

ACCC, 'Online reviews for product and services', https://www.accc.gov.au/business/advertising-and-promotions/online-reviews-for-product-and-services, published and updated 15 July 2026. Supports: incentives for reviews must be disclosed and must not depend on what the review says.

ACMA, 'Avoid sending spam', https://www.acma.gov.au/avoid-sending-spam, no date shown; read 2026-11-04 per the research file. Supports: consent, accurate sender details, and an unsubscribe honoured within five working days.

Housecall Pro, 'Recurring service agreements', https://www.housecallpro.com/resources/recurring-service-agreements/, published 8 June 2026, updated 9 June 2026. Vendor source; no statistics used. Supports: a short follow-up after each completed job about a maintenance plan; define in the contract how unused visits roll over.

Xu, Yu and Tu, Journal of Marketing Research 60(2), 2023, https://research.polyu.edu.hk/en/publications/i-will-get-a-reward-too-when-disclosing-the-referrer-reward-incre/. Supports: stating the referrer's reward in the invitation increased referring across the studies reported. No figures used.

Clayton Utz, 'Referrer beware', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2017/may/referrer-beware-proceed-with-caution-when-contemplating-refer-a-friend-promotions, 11 May 2017 (older than 2022). Supports: a referrer's word alone may not be enough; get the referred person's consent.

Clayton Utz, 'The ACMA cranks up enforcement', https://www.claytonutz.com/insights/2023/november/the-acma-cranks-up-enforcement-do-your-factual-customer-emails-pass-the-spam-act-test, 9 November 2023. Supports: a service reminder that promotes any service can be a commercial message.

OAIC, 'Direct marketing', https://www.oaic.gov.au/privacy/privacy-guidance-for-organisations-and-government-agencies/organisations/direct-marketing, published 1 May 2019, modified 5 September 2024. Supports: APP 7 governs direct marketing using personal information; opt-out must be simple.

Notes: no source in the research covers floor-care maintenance retention or property and strata referral channels (gaps). The intervals are illustrative. The Baylor result is from one experiment. Podium and Housecall Pro are vendor sources.

officialReferences.title: Avoid sending spam
officialReferences.covers: Says commercial messages cannot be sent without the recipient's permission or consent; messages must accurately identify the sender and include correct contact details; every commercial message must contain an unsubscribe option under the Spam Act 2003, which the page says sets out responsibilities under Australian law. Does not mention one-to-one messages. Publisher: ACMA.
